name: The Southern Company
employees: ~29,800 at December 31, 2025 — Georgia Power 7,700, Alabama Power 6,100, Mississippi Power 1,100, Southern Power 500, Southern Company Gas 5,000, Southern Company Services 4,800, Southern Nuclear 3,700 (FY2025 Form 10-K)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Southern Company is the Southeast's regulated gatekeeper for AI load with no grid operator above it and an elected commission beneath it, and it has converted that position into the largest single certification in Georgia's history: 17 GW of contracted large load at July 2026 (Georgia Power 12.5 GW, Alabama Power 4 GW, Mississippi Power 0.5 GW) against a stated 75 GW-plus prospective pipeline it does not count as load; 9,885 MW certified by the Georgia PSC on December 19, 2025 — three combined-cycle blocks, eleven battery projects and 2,821 MW of purchases at about $16.3B of company-owned capital — under a three-year base-rate freeze through 2028 and a shareholder backstop for 2029–2031; an $81B five-year capital plan financed in part by $26.54B of DOE loan guarantees; and a commission whose composition changed on affordability between the certificate's stipulation and its reconsideration, with two more seats on the November 2026 ballot. BACKGROUND. Atlanta; NYSE: SO. Per the FY2025 Form 10-K the system serves 4.59 million retail electric customers (Georgia Power 2.83 million, Alabama Power 1.56 million, Mississippi Power 0.19 million) and about 4.4 million gas customers, employs about 29,800, and owns roughly 45 GW of nameplate generation across the three retail utilities and Southern Power's 12.6 GW contracted fleet; the retail utilities are their own balancing authority outside any RTO. FY2025 adjusted EPS was $4.30 on operating revenue of $29.6B, 2026 guidance is $4.50–4.60 and the company projects 7–8 percent long-term growth from 2028. Georgia Power serves large loads under the PSC's January 2025 rule — 15-year contracts, minimum bills, upstream cost payment, collateral, every contract filed 30 days before signing — with the percentages confidential; Vogtle Units 3 and 4 (2023–2024, $10.670B of Georgia Power net investment, about $3B left with shareholders) are the reason the 2025 certificate contains gas, batteries, purchases and uprates of the older reactors and no new nuclear. Collection gap: the contract percentages, the PPA counterparties, the combined-cycle turbine OEM and the Q3 2026 earnings date were not obtainable from any source found; the dossier says so where it matters rather than filling the space.
ecosystemRole: We assess Southern Company as the utility whose certificate, rather than any customer's lease, decides when the Southeast's AI campuses get power — and as three different counterparties to the sellers in this file at once. Basis: Georgia Power plans, certifies and builds inside a system it balances itself, so there is no capacity auction to bid into and no regional queue; the channels are the company's own certificate (turbines, balance of plant and batteries bought under its supply agreements and fixed-price EPCs), the all-source and storage RFPs (where the bidding developer picks the hardware and the utility picks the bid), and the customer's own supply under the 2026 customer-identified-resource program. For battery sellers it is the rare utility that owns its storage — Wärtsilä at Mossy Branch, Tesla (per trade press) across the 2024 portfolio, Burns & McDonnell and Crowder as EPCs, with 3,022.5 MW more certified in December 2025 and a 500 MW RFP closing in January 2027. For turbine and balance-of-plant sellers it is a buyer that reserved equipment for ten gigawatts before the certificate and ordered the Yates machines two years before the plan. For the hyperscalers and developers it is the counterparty whose 15-year contracts, minimum bills and collateral requirements — $21B-plus by 2028 — set the economics of every campus in Georgia and Alabama, and whose elected commission can reprice the deal at the next election. Per the company's own ladder, the load is 17 GW contracted and 75 GW prospective; the certificate was sized between the two.

productsAndServices.name: Regulated retail electric service — Georgia Power, and the large-load contracting framework
productsAndServices.description: Georgia Power serves approximately 2.8 million retail customers across Georgia (2,834 thousand at December 31, 2025 per the FY2025 Form 10-K) as a vertically integrated utility regulated by the five-member elected Georgia Public Service Commission, which sets its rates, approves its triennial Integrated Resource Plan and certifies each new plant and purchase. The 2025 rate plan, approved by the PSC on July 1, 2025 per the company's 8-K, holds base rates unchanged in 2026, 2027 and 2028 with a retail return-on-equity set point of 10.50 percent inside a 9.50–11.90 percent band and a 56 percent equity ratio; earnings above 11.90 percent are split 40 percent to regulatory assets, 40 percent refunded and 20 percent retained, and a base rate case must be filed by July 1, 2028. Large loads are served under the PSC's January 23, 2025 rule and the company's Rules and Regulations for Electric Service as revised from February 1, 2025: a customer with an expected peak demand of 100 MW or greater may be required to accept 'minimum billing requirements and a longer term of contract', performance and credit provisions, and on termination 'any costs the Company incurred in serving or preparing to serve the customer, including distribution, transmission, and generation costs'. Per the company's Q1 and Q2 2026 investor decks the contracting framework requires at least 15-year terms for data centers (10 years for others), minimum bills covering at least 100 percent of annual incremental cost to serve, termination payments tied to the remaining incremental cost over the contract life, and collateral based on creditworthiness — the company states more than $21B of collateral is required by 2028 with an A+ average counterparty rating. Every contract above 100 MW is filed with the PSC at least 30 days before execution (PSC fact sheet, March 2026).
highlights: PSC's own description of the January 2025 rule: new customers above 100 MW 'can be billed using terms and conditions beyond those used for standard customers', pay 'costs incurred by upstream generation, transmission and distribution … as construction of the data centers progresses', with contract lengths moved 'from 5-year contracts to 15-year contracts' and 'minimum billing requirements' (PSC release, January 23, 2025)

Q2 2026 10-Q: large-load contracts of approximately 11 GW reviewed by state commissions plus approximately 5 GW agreed and awaiting review; 'All … contain minimum bill provisions' and contracts totaling approximately 13 GW 'also contain minimum duration, termination payment requirements, and financial security'

The first contract tested under the 30-day review — OpenAI's ~3,200 MW Effingham County campus, 25-year agreement — cleared on a staff statement in August 2026 with added protections: no recovery of a revenue shortfall from residential customers on early termination, PSC notice within 15 days of any large-customer cancellation, semiannual public reporting (AJC, August 27, 2026)

Base-rate freeze context per The Current: six bill increases in the prior three years; fuel and storm cases excluded from the freeze; a May 2026 fuel-and-storm stipulation then cut the typical residential bill by about $4 a month

Collection gap: the minimum-bill percentages and termination-payment formulas in Georgia's large-load contracts are filed under seal; the company's categories (15-year term, 100 percent of incremental cost, collateral) are the most specific public terms
productsAndServices.positioning: Georgia's framework is a rule plus confidential contracts rather than a published rate class: Dominion Energy Virginia's GS-5 class publishes 85 percent transmission-and-distribution and 60 percent generation minimums and a 14-year term, while Georgia Power's contracts state 15-year terms and minimum bills at 100 percent of incremental cost with the percentages of demand unpublished. Against AEP Ohio's 2025 data-center tariff (85 percent after a ramp, 12-year terms) the Georgia term is longer and the review is case by case. The elected commission and the July 2025 freeze make the political exposure of the framework higher than in appointed-commission states.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct — the utility contracts with the customer under its PSC-approved rules; contracts above 100 MW are filed with the PSC 30 days before execution and reviewed by commission staff.
targetSegments: Hyperscale and self-owned data-center operators (11 GW of the parent's 17 GW contracted at Q2 2026)
Large data-center developers above 300 MW (1.5 GW)
Residential and commercial customers under the frozen base rates
productsAndServices.roadmap: Base rate case due by July 1, 2028; the December 2025 certification order requires the next rate case to show at least $556M a year of downward pressure from large-load revenue in 2029–2031, since raised by the company to approximately $950M a year with the August 2026 contract approvals; a separate PSC hearing on whether a fuel-related regulatory asset should be recovered only from large customers was scheduled to conclude by December 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Certified generation build — the 2025 all-source certification (gas, storage, solar-plus-storage)
productsAndServices.description: On December 19, 2025 the Georgia PSC voted 5–0 to certify, per Georgia Power's 8-K, 'all 9,885 megawatts of requested resources in the All-Source Certification Proceeding … at their respective individual project cost'. The FY2025 Form 10-K breaks the 9,885 MW into 18 RFP resources totaling 7,999 MW (6,804 MW of Georgia Power-owned projects with commercial operation dates from 2028 to 2030), a 50 MW extension of an existing 750 MW affiliate purchase from Mississippi Power through 2029, a 20-year non-affiliate PPA for 930 MW from 2030, five 25-year non-affiliate PPAs totaling 646 MW from 2027, and a 260 MW company-owned battery paired with an existing solar PPA. The company-owned projects carry 'approximately $16.3 billion in projected capital investment (excluding AFUDC)', roughly $14B of it in 2026–2029, and the September and December 2025 certifications together total approximately $16.7B excluding AFUDC. The certified units per the July 31, 2025 request: two combined-cycle units at Plant Bowen (1,482 MW), one at Plant McIntosh (757 MW), two at Plant Wansley (1,453 MW); stand-alone batteries at Bowen (500 MW in two phases), Hammond (192.5 MW phase 2), McIntosh (250 MW), South Hall (250 MW), Thomson (500 MW), Wadley (260 MW), Wansley (500 MW) and Yates (570 MW in two projects); and two solar-plus-storage projects in Laurens County (200 MW + 200 MW) and at Mitchell in Dougherty County (150 MW + 150 MW). The company's build schedule from its earnings decks: 2026 five batteries (765 MW); 2027 Yates Unit 8 (441 MW simple cycle) and two batteries (750 MW); 2028 Yates Units 9–10 (882 MW), five batteries (1,570 MW) and two solar-plus-storage projects (350 MW); 2029 Wansley Unit 10 (777 MW), Bowen Unit 7 (780 MW) and three batteries (610 MW); 2030 McIntosh Unit 12 (797 MW), Bowen Unit 8 (780 MW) and Wansley Unit 11 (777 MW) — 1.2, 1.5, 1.9, 2.3 and 2.8 GW a year with more than 500 miles of new transmission. The Yates simple-cycle units (three Mitsubishi Power M501JAC turbines with VP-X generators, about 1.3 GW) were certified in the 2023 IRP Update; the Unit 9 turbine and generator were delivered in December 2025 for operation by end-2027.
highlights: Execution posture per the Q4 2025 deck: 'All necessary equipment reserved … Turnkey fixed-price EPC agreements in place for project work being performed by external contractors … Internal construction team self-performing McIntosh Unit 12 (CC) and McIntosh BESS … Additional turbines reserved'

Customer-benefit condition in the order: the next base rate case must produce 'downward pressure … of at least $556 million per year' in 2029–2031 from large-load incremental revenue — $8.50 a month for a 1,000 kWh residential customer — and the company 'agreed to financially backstop new projects in years 2029, 2030, and 2031' (PSC release); company-owned projects are subject to PSC construction monitoring

PSC staff had recommended certifying about a third of the request and called the remainder speculative before settling for the whole request; the new commission denied reconsideration 3–2 on February 17, 2026, and a Fulton County petition filed March 25, 2026 seeks decertification of at least 757 MW (Q2 2026 10-Q; AJC)

Prior certifications: 'Through the 2022 IRP and the 2023 IRP Update, the Georgia PSC has certified resources totaling approximately 13 GWs, approximately nine GWs of which are new generation and battery energy storage facilities' at certified costs of $19.5B, in service through 2030 (10-K)

Plant Bowen construction on the two combined-cycle units and a 500 MW battery began July 31, 2026 with the DOE loan package cited; the Wansley units and a 500 MW battery were under construction per the April 2026 release

Collection gap: the combined-cycle turbine OEM and EPCs for Bowen, Wansley and McIntosh are not disclosed in any company or trade-press source found; only the Yates turbines (Mitsubishi Power) and McIntosh self-performance are stated
productsAndServices.positioning: The largest single certification in Georgia's history and, at roughly ten gigawatts against about 22 GW of deployed Georgia Power capacity (PSC fact sheet), close to half the system in one order — against Dominion Energy Virginia's one 944 MW plant certified in 2025. Roughly 60 percent gas by capacity per the AJC. The self-build share (6,804 MW owned) was tested against an all-source RFP with an independent evaluator; the purchased share (2,821 MW of PPAs) went to counterparties the 8-K does not name beyond the Mississippi Power and Southern Power affiliate pieces.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-build into rate base under fixed-price turnkey EPC agreements, with McIntosh Unit 12 and the McIntosh battery self-performed; equipment reserved ahead of certification; recovered through base rates after the 2028 rate case, with the 2029–2031 shareholder backstop.
targetSegments: Georgia Power's retail system, with about 80 percent of the certified capacity expected to serve data centers per the PSC fact sheet
productsAndServices.roadmap: Five batteries in 2026, Yates Unit 8 and two batteries in 2027, Yates 9–10 plus five batteries and two solar-plus-storage projects in 2028, the first two combined-cycle units in 2029, three more in 2030; a further 2,000–6,000 MW of dispatchable capacity for 2032–2033 solicited from June 2026 with certification filings in mid-2027.

productsAndServices.name: Battery energy storage — utility-owned BESS program and the 2025 storage RFP
productsAndServices.description: Georgia Power owns and operates its batteries, which distinguishes it from utilities that procure storage only through developer PPAs. Mossy Branch (65 MW, four hours, Talbot County) reached commercial operation in November 2024 with Wärtsilä as EPC and technology provider (Quantum system, GEMS platform). The 765 MW portfolio under construction per the May 7, 2025 release: Robins 128 MW (Bibb County, June 2026, EPC Burns & McDonnell), Moody 49.5 MW (Lowndes County, co-located with Moody solar, completed ahead of schedule July 2026, EPC Crowder Industrial Construction), Hammond 57.5 MW (Floyd County, November 2026, Crowder), McGrau Ford Phase I 265 MW (Cherokee County, October 2026, Burns & McDonnell) and McGrau Ford Phase II 265 MW (September 2026, Burns & McDonnell). Energy-Storage.news reported in September 2024 that the 2024 portfolio (500 MW / 2,000 MWh — Robins, Moody, Hammond and McGrau Ford II) is supplied under a Tesla Megapack 2XL agreement with a 20-year capacity guarantee, with costs redacted under a PSC rule; the company's own releases name the EPCs but not the battery supplier. A 200 MW four-hour battery in Twiggs County (Crowder) was certified in an expedited proceeding on September 4, 2025 for 2027, and Wadley (260 MW, Jefferson County, Burns & McDonnell, co-located with third-party solar) began construction in March 2026 for 2027. The December 2025 certification added ten stand-alone batteries (3,022.5 MW at eight sites) and two solar-plus-storage projects (350 MW). A separate 2025 Energy Storage System RFP seeks 500 MW of at least two-hour storage online by the end of 2031, with Ascend Analytics as independent evaluator; the 10-K states the RFP was initiated February 11, 2026. Alabama Power's first utility-scale battery — Gorgas, 150 MW two-hour lithium iron phosphate on a retired plant site in Walker County, 92 Tesla Megapacks, completion 2027 — extends the owned-storage model to a second operating company. Southern Power owns 640 MWh of storage in California (Garland 88 MW / 352 MWh and Tranquillity 72 MW / 288 MWh).
highlights: Two of the 765 MW portfolio (Robins and Moody, 178 MW) were in service by April 2026 per the Q2 2026 deck; three more (587 MW) follow in 2026

The 2025 IRP order approved 'more than 1,500 MW' of battery storage by 2035 on top of the certified projects; the certified count after December 2025 is 'nearly 3,000 MW across nine facilities' per the Wadley release

Named EPCs: Burns & McDonnell (Robins, McGrau Ford I and II, Wadley), Crowder Industrial Construction (Moody, Hammond, Twiggs), Wärtsilä (Mossy Branch); battery OEMs for the 2025-certified projects are not disclosed
Storage RFP timeline per the evaluator's schedule reported by Utility Dive: bids in early 2026, short list December 2026, contracts January 2027 — no winners announced at the time of writing
Alabama Power: Tesla Megapacks began arriving at Gorgas in February 2026 per the company's March 2026 article
productsAndServices.positioning: Among the utilities in this file Georgia Power is the one that most consistently buys and owns batteries under its own supply agreements and EPC contracts rather than through developer PPAs — the utility-owned lane that Dominion's 155 MW petition made small and Georgia's certificates made large. Trade press names Tesla as the 2024 portfolio's supplier; Wärtsilä is the one supplier the company itself has named.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility-owned: supply agreement with the battery integrator plus a fixed-price EPC per project, certified into rate base; the 500 MW RFP lane is open to developer bids as well as owned projects.
targetSegments: Georgia Power's own system (peak shaving, the winter peak, integration of the certified solar)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Hammond, McGrau Ford I and II in service by late 2026; Twiggs and Wadley in 2027; the 3,022.5 MW certified in December 2025 in 2026–2030 per the build schedule; the 500 MW RFP contracts in January 2027 for service by 2031; a 200 MW solar + 200 MW storage Laurens County project and a 150 + 150 MW Mitchell project in 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear fleet — Vogtle 3 and 4, the Vogtle 1–2 and Hatch uprates, and Southern Nuclear
productsAndServices.description: Southern Nuclear operates Plant Vogtle (four units, Burke County) and Plant Hatch (two units) for Georgia Power and its co-owners, and Alabama Power's Plant Farley. Vogtle Units 3 and 4, the first new-design reactors built in the United States in a generation (Westinghouse AP1000, approximately 1,117 MW each per Southern Nuclear, ~2,234 MW combined per Georgia Power), reached commercial operation on July 31, 2023 and April 29, 2024. Georgia Power owns 45.7 percent (Oglethorpe Power 30 percent, MEAG Power 22.7 percent, Dalton Utilities 1.6 percent); the FY2025 10-K states 'Georgia Power's final net investment in connection with Plant Vogtle Units 3 and 4 is $10.670 billion, which excludes capitalized AFUDC of approximately $440 million'. The December 2023 PSC cost-recovery order, per GPB, let Georgia Power recover $7.56B of its remaining cost from customers at about $8.95 a month on a typical bill, leaving roughly $3B with shareholders; the all-owner cost was reported at around $35B against the roughly $14B certified in 2009. The company reports 'top decile safety performance and exceptional reliability, with availability factors over 95% since commercial operation' (Q4 2025 deck) and an expected site output above 30 million MWh a year; Unit 4 completed its first refueling outage in September 2025. The NRC issued a White finding on Unit 3 for two 2024 unplanned scrams with complications traced to an over-conservative passive residual heat removal actuation design, returned to Green effective March 20, 2025 (NRC ML25099A013). The 2025 IRP order approved uprates of Vogtle Units 1 and 2 of about 54 MW, some available as early as 2028, and preliminary planning, licensing and engineering for potential Hatch uprates; the NRC renewed Hatch's licences on June 12, 2026 to 2054 and 2058 (Hatch's decade-average capacity factor: 94 percent). The DOE loan guarantees of February 2026 include about 6.3 GW of nuclear uprates and renewals. The chief executive said on the Q2 2026 call, per the Investing.com transcript, that Southern 'is not going to be next' to build an AP1000 while discussing risk-sharing with the federal government and hyperscalers.
highlights: Vogtle 3 and 4 in service July 2023 and April 2024; company availability above 95 percent; Georgia Power net investment $10.670B excluding AFUDC (10-K)

Customer share of the overrun set in the December 2023 order: $7.56B recovered, about $3B to shareholders, +$8.95 a month on a typical bill (GPB); the Vogtle NCCR tariff ceased after Unit 4's commercial operation
NRC White finding on Unit 3 (2024 scrams; PRHR actuation design) closed to Green in March 2025
Vogtle 1–2 uprates of 54 MW approved in the 2025 IRP; Hatch licence renewal June 2026; Hatch preliminary uprate work approved
Collection gap: capacity factors for Units 3 and 4 individually are not published by the company; the 2023 cost-recovery stipulation text was not re-pulled and its terms rest on GPB's report
productsAndServices.positioning: The only utility in this file operating new-build large reactors, and the one whose overrun history most directly explains its appetite: the 2025 certificate contains gas, storage, purchases and uprates of the older units and no new reactor. Dominion holds an SMR memorandum with Amazon at North Anna; Southern's stated position is that it will not be the next AP1000 builder without others sharing the overrun risk.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Regulated generation in Georgia Power's and Alabama Power's rate base; Southern Nuclear operates the plants for the owners; Vogtle 3–4 advanced nuclear production tax credits are monetized with co-owners (Georgia Power paid $131M to co-owners in 2024 per the FY2024 10-K as relayed by trade press).
targetSegments: Georgia Power and Alabama Power retail systems
Co-owners Oglethorpe Power, MEAG Power and Dalton Utilities
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vogtle 1–2 uprates from 2028; Hatch uprate licensing and engineering; licence renewals in the DOE loan package; no new-reactor commitment.

productsAndServices.name: Electric transmission — the ten-year plan, the Ashley Park–Wansley 500 kV line and the DOE-guaranteed grid program
productsAndServices.description: Georgia Power's 2025 IRP included a ten-year transmission plan across 'more than 1,000 miles of transmission lines' (2025 IRP filing and approval releases), and the December 2025 build schedule adds '500+ Miles of New Transmission Lines' tied to the certified plants. The December 2025 Ashley Park project — a new 500/230 kV substation and a 35-mile Ashley Park–Wansley 500 kV line for south metro Atlanta, in service Q2 2028 — is the first named segment. The company's IRP construction and transmission capital footnote in the FY2025 10-K runs about $3.1B, $5.5B, $5.1B, $3.2B and $0.8B for 2026–2030. The February 2026 Department of Energy loan guarantees ($26.54B — Georgia Power $22.4B, Alabama Power $4.1B; draws through September 2033 at Treasury plus 37.5 basis points, maturing December 2055) cover, per Utility Dive's reading of the DOE package, 5.3 GW of new gas including Yates, about 500 MW of gas uprates, 6.3 GW of nuclear uprates and renewals, 1 GW of hydro, storage and more than 1,300 miles of transmission and distribution, with the company citing about $7B of customer savings. Fortune reported in July 2026 that the expansion spans more than 330 parcels with five eminent-domain uses in the prior year and that 70–80 percent of the new power will serve AI data centers.
highlights: Ten-year transmission plan of more than 1,000 miles approved with the 2025 IRP; 500-plus miles tied to the certified 2026–2030 build
Ashley Park 500/230 kV substation and Ashley Park–Wansley 500 kV line, Q2 2028
DOE loan guarantees of $26.54B closed February 2026 — the largest in the department's history per Utility Dive — at Treasury + 37.5 bp with about $300M a year of interest savings
Quarterly large-load reporting and semi-annual transmission updates to PSC staff were added by the 2025 IRP stipulation (POWER)
productsAndServices.positioning: Unlike Dominion, whose 500 kV and 765 kV lines are planned and cost-allocated through PJM's regional process, Georgia Power plans and builds its own transmission as its own balancing authority; the cost enters rate base directly and the routing fights are the company's alone.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-build into rate base; the DOE loan guarantees finance the program at below-market cost.
targetSegments: Georgia Power's system, with the certified plants and the data-center load centers (metro Atlanta, Effingham and the I-16 and I-75 corridors) as the drivers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Ashley Park–Wansley 2028; the 500-plus miles tied to the certified plants through 2030; DOE draws through 2033.

productsAndServices.name: Alabama Power and Mississippi Power — the other two retail utilities
productsAndServices.description: Alabama Power serves 1,563 thousand retail customers and Mississippi Power 193 thousand (December 31, 2025, FY2025 10-K), both under appointed commissions with annual rate-stabilization mechanisms. Alabama Power's December 2, 2025 order holds Rate RSE flat through 2027 and defers recovery of the Lindsay Hill Generating Station — a gas combined-cycle plant of about 880–895 MW acquired September 30, 2025 after an Alabama PSC certificate of August 13, 2025 — to January 2028 billings; its first utility-scale battery (Gorgas, 150 MW, 92 Tesla Megapacks) completes in 2027, and Barry Unit 5's coal-to-gas conversion is scheduled for 2026–2028. The parent's Q2 2026 deck attributes 4 GW of its 17 GW of contracted large load to Alabama Power in three projects; the Energy and Policy Institute reports that Alabama Power's contracts filed in June–August 2026 for Meta (Dotier LLC), Nebius/Alabama ADC and Woostor carry redacted terms, minimum bills and megawatts, and that the Alabama PSC opened a generic large-load docket on July 8, 2026 under a 2026 statute (SB 270) effective October 1, 2026 for loads of 150 MW or more. Mississippi Power acquired FP&L's 50 percent of Plant Daniel Units 1 and 2 on July 30, 2025, extended the Daniel 2 and Watson 4 retirements in a March 2026 IRP update, received Mississippi PSC approval on July 7, 2026 to convert Daniel Unit 1 or 2 to gas by 2029, supplies Georgia Power under a 750 MW affiliate PPA extended in part through 2029, and reports 'recently signed economic development loads of approximately 600 MWs' including the Compass Datacenters $10B, ~500 MW Meridian campus (2025 Year in Review; Q2 2026 10-Q).
highlights: Alabama Power: Lindsay Hill CC acquired September 2025; Rate RSE flat through 2027; Gorgas BESS 2027; 4 GW of the parent's contracted large load in three projects (Q2 2026 deck)
Alabama large-load contracts (Meta/Dotier, Nebius, Woostor) filed with terms redacted; a generic Alabama PSC docket opened July 2026 (EPI, NBC 15)

Mississippi Power: Plant Daniel 50 percent acquisition July 2025; gas conversion of one Daniel unit approved July 2026; 0.5 GW of the parent's contracted large load; Compass Datacenters ~500 MW Meridian campus
Grist reported in August 2024 that the Plant Daniel PPA to Georgia Power keeps two coal units open at about $3 per kilowatt-year
productsAndServices.positioning: Alabama Power is the second large-load market in the system (4 GW contracted) under an appointed commission with a new large-load statute; Mississippi Power is the smallest of the three retail utilities and a capacity supplier to Georgia Power.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct regulated retail service; affiliate PPAs to Georgia Power approved by FERC and the Georgia PSC.
targetSegments: Alabama and southeast Mississippi retail customers
Data-center customers in Alabama (Meta, Nebius, Woostor per EPI) and Mississippi (Compass Datacenters)
Georgia Power as an affiliate purchaser
productsAndServices.roadmap: Alabama PSC large-load rules from October 2026; Lindsay Hill in Rate CNP from January 2028; Daniel gas conversion 2029.

productsAndServices.name: Southern Power — the contracted wholesale fleet, gas uprates and brownfield options
productsAndServices.description: Southern Power owns 12,648 MW in commercial operation (FY2025 10-K) sold under long-term contracts to utilities and corporate buyers, including 732 MW of affiliate PPAs in the December 2025 Georgia certification and two FERC-approved affiliate PPAs with Georgia Power (638 MW and 74 MW) that began in June 2026 under the 2022 IRP. Per the Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 decks and the Q2 2026 10-Q it holds 640 MWh of storage in California (Garland and Tranquillity), the 512 MW Millers Branch solar project in Texas (phase I of 200 MW in service February 2026), a 1 GW wind repowering program, committed gas-turbine uprates at Franklin (Alabama, 300 MW) and Wansley (Georgia, 100 MW) of about $700M for 2029–2031, is pursuing up to 700 MW of capacity uprates, and is evaluating gas generation at six brownfield sites. Chris Cummiskey, the parent's chief commercial officer, chairs it.
highlights: 12,648 MW contracted fleet; 732 MW of affiliate PPAs certified for Georgia Power in December 2025; 638 MW and 74 MW affiliate PPAs from June 2026
Gas uprates at Franklin and Wansley (400 MW, ~$700M, 2029–2031); up to 700 MW of uprates under evaluation; six brownfield gas sites
Millers Branch solar 512 MW (Texas) in phases through 2026; 1 GW wind repowering
productsAndServices.positioning: The system's contracted, non-rate-base lane — the counterparty through which Georgia Power's certificates can include affiliate purchases and the vehicle for turbine uprates the retail utilities do not own.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term PPAs with affiliates and third parties; FERC-jurisdictional wholesale sales.
targetSegments: Georgia Power and other Southern utilities under affiliate PPAs
productsAndServices.roadmap: Franklin and Wansley uprates 2029–2031; brownfield gas evaluations; further solar phases in 2026.

productsAndServices.description: Southern Company Gas serves approximately 4.4 million natural gas customers in Illinois, Georgia, Virginia and Tennessee (Q4 2025 deck) and holds the SNG pipeline partnership with Kinder Morgan whose South System Expansion is in the Q4 2025 deck. The FY2025 capital plan allocates about $9B of the $81B five-year total to the gas utilities, against $68B for the electric utilities; the parent describes 95 percent of the plan as state-regulated.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Southern Company's large-load story is one of the most disciplined in the sector in its vocabulary and one of the most exposed in its politics. Basis: since Q3 2025 the parent has published a four-tranche ladder — contracted, finalizing, late-stage, prospective — with a written definition of 'contracted' (a fully executed agreement submitted to or reviewed by the state regulator) and a separate Georgia-only 'committed' figure for signed requests for service; the contracted figure rose from 8 GW to 17 GW in three quarters while the 75 GW prospective figure was never counted as load. The exposure is that the body reading those figures is elected: the commission that certified 9,885 MW five to nothing in December 2025 denied reconsideration three to two two months later after two seats changed hands on affordability, and two more seats are on the November 2026 ballot with data-center overbuilding a stated issue.

(High confidence) We assess that Georgia Power's certificate, not any customer's contract, is the instrument that converts the pipeline into equipment orders, and that the purchasing decisions were made a year or more before it. Basis: the Yates turbines were ordered around the 2023 update and delivered in December 2025 for a plan approved in July 2025; the 2024 battery portfolio's supplier and EPCs were named in 2024–2025 for a portfolio certified in 2022 and expanded in 2025; the Q4 2025 deck states all equipment for the ten-gigawatt build is reserved under fixed-price turnkey EPCs; and the next solicitation (2,000–6,000 MW for 2032–2033) opened in June 2026 with certification in mid-2027. A seller's calendar in Georgia is the RFP and the reservation, not the docket.

(High confidence) We assess that Georgia Power is the utility in this file most likely to buy a battery itself rather than through a developer, and that this is structural rather than incidental. Basis: Mossy Branch, the 765 MW portfolio, Twiggs and Wadley are all company-owned under supply agreements and named EPCs (Burns & McDonnell, Crowder, Wärtsilä), the December 2025 certificate added 3,022.5 MW of owned stand-alone storage against 2,821 MW of purchases of all kinds, and the 2025 IRP's storage target exceeds 1,500 MW by 2035 on top of that. The 500 MW storage RFP is the developer lane; it is smaller than the owned lane by an order of magnitude.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the December 2025 backstop and the OpenAI-contract protections mark a shift from tariff design to political guarantee, and that the shift will be tested in the 2028 rate case rather than before. Basis: the certificate's condition requires at least $556M a year of downward residential pressure in 2029–2031 — which the company has since restated as about $950M a year with the August 2026 contract approvals — and the freeze defers base-rate costs to a case that must be filed by July 2028, so the deferred costs, the new plants and the end of the backstop meet in one proceeding. The court petition and the fuel-clause hearing on large-customer allocation are the interim tests; the moderate confidence reflects that the backstop's enforcement mechanism (suspension or alteration of certification if contracts fail to materialize) has not been exercised.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Vogtle's history has fixed the company's technology appetite for the rest of the decade: proven gas turbines from one OEM at existing sites, lithium iron phosphate batteries from established integrators, uprates of the existing reactors, and no first-of-a-kind commitment. Basis: the 2025 IRP and certificate contain no new reactor; the chief executive's July 2026 statement that Southern 'is not going to be next' to build an AP1000 without others sharing the overrun risk; the $10.670B net investment and the ~$3B shareholder loss recorded in the 10-K and the 2023 recovery order; and a DOE loan package whose nuclear content is uprates and renewals. The moderate confidence reflects the company's stated talks with the federal government and hyperscalers on risk-sharing, which could reopen the question.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the Southeast's lack of an RTO makes Georgia Power's own forecast the single point of failure for the plan, and that the reporting conditions attached in 2025 are the commission's substitute for a regional check. Basis: the IRP stipulation added quarterly large-load reports and semi-annual transmission updates; staff testimony in November 2025 put executed-contract support at about 1,900 MW when the certificate was requested; an SELC-commissioned model put a 1-in-500 probability on needing 10 GW; and the pipeline lost 14.3 GW of exited projects in a year. Against that, the contracted tranche has grown every quarter since, so the forecast's credibility is improving with the ladder rather than with the model.

(Low confidence) We assess that the turbine OEM for the Bowen, Wansley and McIntosh combined-cycle units is the same J-class supplier as Yates, on the basis that the Q4 2025 deck describes 'additional turbines reserved' and no second OEM appears in any filing or release. No source states it; treat as inference until a groundbreaking release names the equipment.

Collection gap: the minimum-bill percentages, termination formulas and contracted megawatts in Georgia's large-load contracts are filed under seal; the rule's formal citation was not confirmed in any PSC document found; the eleven PPA counterparties in the December 2025 certificate are unnamed beyond the affiliate pieces; capacity factors for Vogtle Units 3 and 4 are not published; and the Q3 2026 earnings date was not company-confirmed. INDICATORS TO WATCH. October 29, 2026 (expected, not company-confirmed) — Q3 2026 results: a contracted figure above 17 GW with Georgia Power's share above 12.5 GW would confirm Judgment 1's ladder is still converting; a flat contracted figure beside a rising prospective one would not. November 3, 2026 — Georgia PSC general election (Districts 3 and 5): a 3–2 Democratic majority would make the fuel-clause allocation hearing and the 2028 rate case the venue for Judgment 4; a Republican hold keeps the certificate's terms as written. December 2026 — storage RFP short list and the PSC's large-customer allocation hearing; January 2027 — storage contracts: a developer winner other than the company's existing EPCs would widen the battery lane. Mid-2027 — certification filing for the 2032–2033 request: a self-build share above two-thirds would confirm Judgment 2; a PPA-heavy filing would indicate the commission has begun preferring purchases. First groundbreaking release naming the Bowen or Wansley turbine OEM — resolves Judgment 7. Fulton County ruling on the certification petition — a decertification of the McIntosh block would be the first reversal of a Georgia certificate in this cycle.

relationships.note: Dominion Energy Virginia's GS-5 class and Georgia Power's large-load rule are the two Southeastern templates for binding data-center customers; the dossiers compare their terms directly.
relationships.context: The Georgia framework (15-year contracts, minimum bills at 100 percent of incremental cost, confidential percentages, contracts filed 30 days before signing) and Virginia's GS-5 class (14-year terms, published 85 percent transmission-and-distribution and 60 percent generation minimums, effective January 2027) are the reference points regulators and trade press cite against each other; the two utilities do not compete for customers, but they compete for the same hyperscale capital and set each other's terms.

policyExposure.regime: Georgia PSC large-load rule (contracts above 100 MW)
policyExposure.exposure: Every new Georgia Power customer above 100 MW is served on extended terms — 15-year contracts, minimum bills, payment for upstream generation, transmission and distribution, termination payments, collateral — and every such contract is filed with the PSC at least 30 days before execution; the OpenAI contract cleared this review in August 2026 with added protections. Alabama's 2026 statute (150 MW threshold, effective October 1, 2026) and generic docket extend the model to Alabama Power.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company's stated framework: at least 15-year terms, minimum bills at 100 percent of incremental cost, termination payments, $21B-plus of collateral by 2028, and the July 2026 Customer Protection Pledge.

policyExposure.regime: Federal clean-energy credits (ITC/45X, nuclear PTC) after the 2025 reconciliation act
policyExposure.exposure: The company's storage and nuclear programs rely on transferable credits: Georgia Power paid $131M to Vogtle co-owners in 2024 for advanced nuclear production tax credits per the FY2024 10-K as relayed by trade press, and the 2024 battery portfolio was planned with IRA credits per Energy-Storage.news. Analyses of the July 2025 act cited by the research indicate the storage credit phase-out does not apply to energy-storage technology and nuclear credits were largely preserved; the company has not quantified the effect in the sources found.
policyExposure.mitigation: The DOE loan guarantees of February 2026 ($26.54B) and continued use of third-party credit transfers per the 10-K.

policyExposure.regime: EPA power-plant rules (mercury and air toxics, greenhouse-gas standards)
policyExposure.exposure: The 2025 IRP keeps Plants Bowen and Scherer's coal units running through at least 2034 with gas co-firing and environmental controls; the EPA granted both plants two-year exemptions from the mercury rule in April 2025.
policyExposure.mitigation: Gas co-firing at Bowen 1–4 and Scherer, and the certified combined-cycle replacements from 2029.

policyExposure.regime: Georgia data-center sales-tax exemption and 2026 cost-shift bills
policyExposure.exposure: The state's data-center sales-and-use tax exemption runs through December 31, 2031; the 2026 session's bills to end it, to move data-center costs off other customers (SB 34) or to impose a moratorium all died, so the commission's contracts remain the only cost-allocation instrument.

$26.54B of federal loan guarantees (Georgia Power $22.4B, Alabama Power $4.1B) at Treasury plus 37.5 basis points, drawn through September 2033 and maturing December 2055, finance the certified gas, nuclear-uprate, hydro, storage and transmission program with about $300M a year of interest savings per Utility Dive.
